text:
alex: Heads-up — around 10:12 UTC we saw ~3% of us-west requests for tenant:acme get routed to eu-west variant-quant-2 after prefetch. Latency spiked for those sessions. Anyone touching routing rules or prefetch behavior?

maya: I noticed the same in the console traces, small but reproducible. The request traces show X-Prefetch=true + region_affinity=us-west, but final target was eu-west. Posting a short log snippet: 
```
[2026-03-17T10:12:13Z] req=7f2a tenant=acme src_region=us-west prefetched=true route_decision=EVALUATE -> redirect_target=eu-west:variant-quant-2
```

liam: Could that be the tiered fallback kicking in? If the local variant was temporarily at capacity we might be ejected to aux regions. But 3% is weirdly high. Did quota gates open?

eva: We rolled tenant-prefetch feature yesterday morning (canary -> all). Prefetch sets X-Prefetch header and also temporarily relaxes routing constraints to allow warmup traffic to go to spare capacity. Looks like that relaxation includes cross-region allowlists. That's probably the cause.

alex: @eva can you confirm whether prefetch implicitly overrides "local_only" routing flag for variants? If so that's a bug.

eva: yes, in the initial implementation prefetch uses route_policy=warmup which has allow_cross_region=true to find warm GPUs. I can see how that interacts poorly with tenant-level locality requirements.

maya: Dumped the decision tree for req=7f2a: 
```
input: {tenant:acme, x-prefetch:1, src_region:us-west, tier:paid}
step1: check tenant pins -> none
step2: capacity check local variant-quant-1 -> reported 0 available for immediate slot
step3: warmup policy (x-prefetch) -> allow_cross_region=true -> pick eu-west:variant-quant-2
step4: route and start kvcache warmup
```

liam: Hmm capacity=0 sounds wrong. Could be a transient drain combined with a mis-read of buffer capacity metric. But we shouldn't break tenant locality for paid customers.

alex: short mitigation: can we flip the prefetch warmup policy to respect tenant.local_only=true ? Or set prefetch.cross_region=false for paid tenants?

eva: I'll push a hotfix to the policy: prefetch.warmup_respect_local=true and patch canary immediately. Will set default for paid tenants to false.

route-bot: Patch proposal created: RFC-2982 prefetch locality change, PR #4821.

maya: Quick manual rollback option: applied routing override for tenant=acme -> enforce local_only on the routing controller. Doing it now.

alex: Thanks. Can we also add a telemetry tag so we can query how many requests used warmup.allow_cross_region in the past 24h? Need to measure blast radius.

liam: I'll add a dashboard tile and a short alert for >0.5% cross-region warmups for paid tenants.

deploy-bot: release 2026.03.17.4 deployed to canary at 10:34 UTC: prefetch.warmup_respect_local=true (canary).

maya: Canary looks good, acme routing back to local. No more cross-region hits in the sample window.

eva: Rolling to prod in 5m. Also adding unit test to prevent prefetch from flipping locality for tenants with local_only pin.

alex: Nice catch everyone. Follow-ups: 1) dashboard tile + alert (liam), 2) telemetry backfill to measure past 7 days (maya), 3) postmortem note in incidents channel if we cross threshold (I'll draft). :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: release 2026.03.17.4 rolled to prod at 10:41 UTC.

maya: Closing thread, we'll track in RFC-2982 and incident tracker if needed.
